author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Dick's own 1974 screenplay adaptation of his novel Ubik, an unfilmed script in which he reworked the book's collapsing realities and half-life world for the screen.
page_summary:
This is Philip K. Dick's own screenplay adaptation of Ubik, written in 1974 and never produced. Adapting one of his most admired novels himself, Dick translated its central conceits, the half-life state in which the dead persist in fading consciousness, the entropic decay of reality signaled by regressing objects, and the mysterious reality-stabilizing substance Ubik, into film form, making choices about structure and emphasis that differ from the novel.

Because the script was never filmed, it survives as a literary curiosity and a document of Dick's relationship to cinema, showing how he imagined his own difficult material reaching the screen. It gives readers a rare chance to see him revising and re-seeing his fiction in a different medium, on the eve of the 1974 experiences that would reshape his later work.

The portal holds two archive manifestations, the fuller running to well over two hundred pages, reflecting the screenplay's eventual publication. It is best read alongside the novel Ubik and the portal's records for Dick's film-related material.
